full_judgment:
The pre-emptor filed the pre-emption Case No. 37 of 2003 before the Assistant Judge, Wazirpur, Barisal under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against the opposite parties stating that father of the pre-emptor was the owner of one acre of land in SA Khatian Nos. 724, 730 and 589 and the same has been recorded in his name and he has been died during the possession of the case land. The father of the pre-emptor died leaving behind his one son Taib Ali (pre-emptor) and five daughters. One son gets 28 decimals of land and one daughter gets 14 decimals of land. The first daughter transferred her land to the pre-emptee No. 8 by her deed dated 3-11-99. Daughter Hachenbhanu transferred her land to the Pre-emptee Nos. 6 and 7 by her deed dated 17-4.94. Daughter Khatunbhanu transferred her land to the pre-emptor Taib Ali Mridha and Meher Nega is the pre-emptee No. 9. The heirs of the pre-emptor and purchasers are possession in total 42 decimals of land of three khatians. Shohorbhanu died leaving behind her three sons and one daughter and they have been owner of the 14 decimals land and they are the pre-emptee Nos. 2-5 of the instant case and they are also nephews of the pre-emptor. On 23-4-2003 the sellers transferred 15 decimals of land to the pre-emptee No.1 (purchaser) by registered deed is valued in cash of Taka 98,000. In the meantime the pre-emptor did not know about the matter. On 3-5-2003 at first the pre-emptor knew the facts through A. Karim. On 6-5-2003 the pre-emptor searched the Wazirpur Sub-Registry office and obtained the certified copy of the kabala. The pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance of the jama. The Kabala purchaser No.1 is a stranger and no notice has been served upon the pre-emptor and he did not know at al. The pre-emptor cultivated three biggas land and the said land is the homestead of the pre-emptor. Hence, this case. 

 14. On perusal of records, it appears that the pre-emptor-opposite party to prove their case produced Taib Ali Mridha and Md. Abul Hossain as PTW 1 and PTW 2 and PTW 1 and PTW 2 proved the deed dated 23-4-2003 as Exhibit-1 and certified copy of SA Khatian No. 724/730/89 as Exhibit-2 series. On the other hand, the pre-emptee-petitioner produced 3 witnesses namely, Md. Shahidul Islam Mrdha as OPW 1, Shah Alam as OPW 2 and Md. Kadam Ali Hang as OPW 3. OPW 2 proved the original deed No. 1431 dated 23-4-03 and original deed No. 3695 dated 22-11-04 as Exhibit-Ka series A. Later on the pre-emptor-opposite party proved 4 more deeds as Exhibit-3 series. 

 15. It appears from the records that the father of pre-emptor-opposite party Taib Ali Mrida was the registered owner of the suit land and the pre-emptor-opposite party as the heir of his father got property in the land of 3 Khatians. Therefore, it is proved that the pre-emptor-opposite party are the co-sharers of the suit land by inheritance.
